title: Quadratic Equations and Functions
subtitle: Factor quadratics, use the quadratic formula, interpret roots and vertices, and solve quadratic models.

isi.content: A quadratic equation contains a squared variable and can be written in standard form as \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), where \(a\ne0\). Its graph is a parabola.

items.title: Opens upward
items.content: If \(a>0\), the parabola opens upward and has a minimum.

items.title: Opens downward
items.content: If \(a<0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum.

items.title: Roots
items.content: The real solutions of the equation are the x-intercepts of the graph.

isi.content: Before solving, move every term to one side so the equation equals zero. Then identify \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) carefully, including their signs.
\[AB=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad A=0\text{ or }B=0\]
Factoring rewrites a quadratic as a product. Once the product equals zero, set each factor equal to zero.

isi.title: Example: monic quadratic
isi.content: For \(x^2-7x+12=0\), the numbers \(-3\) and \(-4\) multiply to 12 and add to \(-7\). Thus \((x-3)(x-4)=0\), giving \(x=3\) or \(x=4\).
Factoring is often the fastest method when the coefficients are small and the factors are easy to recognize.
\[x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\]

items: Write the equation in the form \(ax^2+bx+c=0\).
Substitute into the formula using parentheses.
Simplify the radical and reduce the resulting fractions.

isi.title: Example: use the formula
isi.content: For \(3x^2+12x+6=0\), \(a=3\), \(b=12\), and \(c=6\). The formula gives \(x=\dfrac{-12\pm\sqrt{72}}{6}=-2\pm\sqrt2\).
Keep exact radical answers unless the question requests a decimal approximation.

materi.judul: The discriminant and number of solutions

isi.title: Example: exactly one real solution
isi.content: For \(x^2+3x+2.25=0\), \(D=3^2-4(1)(2.25)=0\). Therefore, the equation has one repeated real solution, \(x=-\dfrac32\).

isi.title: Example: parameter with no real solutions
isi.content: For \(2x^2-4x=t\), rewrite as \(2x^2-4x-t=0\). Then \(D=16+8t\). No real solutions require \(16+8t<0\), so \(t<-2\).

materi.judul: Axis of symmetry and the vertex

isi.content: The axis of symmetry passes through the vertex. If the roots are \(r_1\) and \(r_2\), the axis is also the midpoint of the roots:

isi.title: Example: vertex from standard form
isi.content: For \(P(x)=-2x^2+160x-1200\), the vertex x-coordinate is \(-\dfrac{160}{2(-2)}=40\). Substituting gives \(P(40)=2000\), the maximum profit.

isi.title: Example: vertex from factored form
isi.content: For \(y=a(x-2)(x+4)\), the roots are 2 and \(-4\), so the axis is \(x=\dfrac{2+(-4)}2=-1\). Then the vertex y-coordinate is \(a(-3)(3)=-9a\).
Quadratic models can describe area, profit, projectile height, subscriber growth, and other situations with a changing rate.

isi.title: Example: projectile motion
isi.content: For \(h(t)=-4.9t^2+25t\), the object is on the ground when \(h(t)=0\). The solution \(t=0\) represents launch, while the positive solution represents the later landing time.

isi.title: Example: maximum area
isi.content: A garden against a fence has area \(A(x)=x(80-2x)=-2x^2+80x\). The vertex occurs at \(x=20\), giving maximum area \(A(20)=800\) square feet.

items: Reject negative time, negative length, or other impossible contextual values.
Use the vertex for a maximum or minimum when the model is quadratic.
Interpret each root in the context instead of automatically keeping every algebraic solution.

isi.content: If a quadratic has roots \(r_1\) and \(r_2\), it can be written as \(f(x)=a(x-r_1)(x-r_2)\). The value of \(a\) controls the vertical stretch and whether the parabola opens up or down.

isi.title: Example: find a from a point
isi.content: Suppose the roots are \(-2\) and 6 and the graph passes through \((2,-16)\). Then \(f(x)=a(x+2)(x-6)\). Since \(-16=a(4)(-4)=-16a\), we get \(a=1\).
The sum of the roots is \(-\dfrac ba\), and the product of the roots is \(\dfrac ca\). These relationships can provide a fast alternative to solving.

items: Move all terms to one side and set the equation equal to zero.
Try factoring, especially for small integer coefficients.
If factoring is not efficient, use the quadratic formula.
Use the discriminant when only the number of real solutions is requested.
Use the vertex or axis of symmetry for maximum and minimum questions.
Check roots in the original equation and reject values that do not fit the context.
Use Desmos to verify roots, vertices, and intersections when helpful.

isi.content: The leading coefficient determines the direction of the parabola: positive means a minimum, negative means a maximum.

latihan.question: If \(t>0\) and \(t^2-4=0\), what is the value of \(t\)?
The profit, in dollars, from selling \(x\) tickets is modeled by \(P(x)=-2x^2+160x-1200\). What is the maximum possible profit?
discussion: The parabola opens downward because the coefficient of \(x^2\) is negative.
The maximum possible profit is USD 2,000, choice B.

latihan.question: What are the solutions to \(3x^2+12x+6=0\)?
discussion: Use the quadratic formula with \(a=3\), \(b=12\), and \(c=6\).
Since \(\sqrt{72}=6\sqrt2\), the solutions are \(-2\pm\sqrt2\), choice A.

latihan.question: Given \(y=a(x-2)(x+4)\), where \(a\) is nonzero, the graph has vertex \((c,d)\). Which expression equals \(d\)?
discussion: The roots are 2 and \(-4\), so the axis of symmetry is \(x=-1\).
Therefore, the vertex y-coordinate is \(d=-9a\), choice A.

latihan.question: A rectangular garden is built against a fence. Three sides require fencing, with 80 feet available. If \(x\) is the width perpendicular to the fence, the area is \(A(x)=x(80-2x)\). What is the maximum possible area?
discussion: The maximum area is 800 square feet, choice C.

latihan.question: Given \(2x^2-4x=t\), where \(t\) is a constant, if the equation has no real solutions, which could be the value of \(t\)?
discussion: Only \(-3\) satisfies this condition, choice A.

latihan.question: Given \(x^2+x-12=0\), if \(a\) is a solution and \(a>0\), what is \(a\)?
The height of a ball is modeled by \(h(t)=-16t^2+80t+96\). A drone is at a constant height of 180 feet. For how many values of \(t\) will the ball be at the same height?
discussion: Its discriminant is \((-20)^2-4(4)(21)=64>0\), so there are two real values of \(t\).

latihan.question: A parabola has x-intercepts at \(x=4\) and \(x=10\). Its vertex has y-coordinate \(-18\). Which equation could define it?
discussion: The axis of symmetry is the midpoint of the roots: \(x=7\).
To make the vertex y-coordinate \(-18\), multiply by 2: \(y=2(x-4)(x-10)\).

latihan.question: Subscriber gain is modeled by \(S(x)=-5x^2+300x+1500\), where \(x\) is thousands of dollars spent on advertising. The company wants at least 5,500 subscribers. Which spending amount could work?
discussion: Evaluate the model using \(x\) in thousands of dollars.
Thus, USD 20,000 could work. The correct answer is C.

latihan.question: Let \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\). The graph has x-intercepts \(-2\) and \(6\), and passes through \((2,-16)\). What is \(a+b+c\)?
A company's profit is modeled by \(P(x)=-(x-12)^2+81\). For what range of \(x\) is profit at least 45 thousand dollars?
discussion: Set the profit greater than or equal to 45: \(-(x-12)^2+81\ge45\).
Multiply by \(-1\) and reverse the sign: \((x-12)^2\le36\).
Thus, \(-6\le x-12\le6\), so \(6\le x\le18\), choice A.

latihan.question: Let \(f(x)=x^2-kx+28\). The graph intersects the x-axis at two distinct integer values. Which could be \(k\)?
discussion: The integer roots must multiply to 28, and their sum must equal \(k\).
The factor pair \(4\) and \(7\) has sum 11 and gives two distinct integer roots.

latihan.question: Let \(f(x)=x^2+bx+c\). The graph intersects the x-axis at \(x=3\) and \(x=12\). What is \(f(2)\)?

Subscribers are modeled by \(N(p)=8000-100p\). The company has a fixed monthly cost of USD \(60{,}000\) and an additional USD \(20\) cost per subscriber. What subscription price maximizes monthly profit?
discussion: The subscription price that maximizes profit is USD 50, choice C.

latihan.question: The area of a triangle is 270 square centimeters. Its base is 12 centimeters greater than its height. What is the height?
discussion: Let the height be \(h\), so the base is \(h+12\).
Factor or use the quadratic formula to get \(h=18\) or \(h=-30\). A length must be positive, so the height is 18 centimeters.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=(x+7)^2+4\), for what value of \(x\) does \(f(x)\) reach its minimum?
discussion: The function is in vertex form \(f(x)=(x-h)^2+k\).
Here, \(x+7=x-(-7)\), so the vertex x-coordinate is \(-7\).
Because the squared term is nonnegative, the minimum occurs at \(x=-7\).

latihan.question: The function gives the product of \(x\) and a number 91 greater than \(x\). Which equation defines \(f\)?
discussion: The number that is 91 greater than \(x\) is \(x+91\).

latihan.question: Given \(4x^2+bx-45=(hx+k)(x+j)\), where \(h\), \(k\), and \(j\) are integers, which must be an integer?
discussion: Since \(k\) and \(j\) are integers and \(kj=-45\), \(k\) is an integer divisor of 45.
Therefore, \(\dfrac{45}{k}\) must be an integer, choice D.

latihan.question: Given \(f(x)=x^2-40x+2304\), what is the minimum value of \(f(x)\)?
discussion: The squared term is at least 0, so the minimum occurs when \(x=20\).

additionalPractice.question: Factor \(x^2+5x+6\).
discussion: The numbers 2 and 3 multiply to 6 and add to 5.

additionalPractice.question: How many real solutions does \(x^2+4=0\) have?
discussion: No real number has a square equal to a negative value.
Therefore, there are 0 real solutions, choice A.

additionalPractice.question: Solve \(x^2-7x+12=0\).
discussion: Set each factor equal to zero: \(x=3\) or \(x=4\).

additionalPractice.question: For \(y=(x-2)(x+6)\), find the axis of symmetry.
discussion: The axis of symmetry is their midpoint: \(x=\dfrac{2+(-6)}2=-2\).

additionalPractice.question: The equation \(x^2+kx+16=0\) has exactly one real solution. Which could be the value of \(k\)?
discussion: Exactly one real solution requires discriminant 0.
Among the choices, 8 works, choice C.

additionalPractice.question: A ball's height is \(h(t)=-16t^2+80t+5\). Find the positive time when it hits the ground, to the nearest tenth of a second.
discussion: Set the height equal to zero: \(-16t^2+80t+5=0\).
The positive solution is approximately \(5.06\), which rounds to 5.1 seconds.

additionalPractice.question: If \(x^2-10x+c=0\) has roots that differ by 4, find \(c\).
discussion: The roots have sum 10 and differ by 4.
